Speaking with the Pittsburgh-Gazette’s Gerry Dulac, Steelers president Art Rooney II said Aaron Rodgers was not a “good teammate” following his release.
items.text: In a story published by Dulac on Thursday, Rooney said the Steelers are “100 percent” committed to head coach Mike McCarthy, while adding that “insubordination will not be tolerated” as far as Rodgers is concerned. According to Dulac, Rodgers and McCarthy met on Tuesday night, just hours before the QB’s benching, and presented McCarthy with an ultimatum: “let me call the plays or just release me.” What followed from there was Rodgers’ benching and eventual release after he went scorched earth on the Steelers and McCarthy on the Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday. items.title: Speaking on NFL GameDay Morning, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Brock Purdy is considered day-to-day with his ankle injury.
items.text: Purdy suffered a sprained ankle in the Niners’ Week 11 win over the Vikings and was a DNP on Wednesday. Rapoport reports the injury is thought to be “minor,” but noted that whether or not Purdy suits up for Week 12 against the Seahawks “remains to be seen.” Given the importance of the divisional matchup, it’s hard to imagine Purdy sitting at this point. We’ll see how his next two practices go to close out the week, but this doesn’t sound like something we need to be too concerned about just yet. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Christian Watson has entered the league’s concussion protocol.
items.text: Watson exited in the second quarter of Wednesday’s game against the Rams after taking a helmet-to-helmet hit from Rams safety Kamren Kinchens. The hard hit left Watson on the ground for an extended period before he eventually got up on his own and went to the locker room. Watson was ruled out after halftime and now has to clear concussion protocol to play in Week 13’s game against the Saints. With extended time to clear protocol, Watson should have a decent chance of clearing protocol. We will be tracking his practice status throughout next week. - Zachary Krueger

items.text: Parkinson somehow lost a yard on two reception despite the team losing both Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen to injury, the latter of whom departed in the first half and the former of whom left at the beginning of the fourth quarter. The Rams completely controlled the flow of the game after Packers receiver Christian Watson departed with a concussion following a vicious targeting hit down the sideline just before the half, eventually leading to 47 total team carries to just 23 Matthew Stafford pass attempts. items.title: Konata Mumpfield caught 4-of-5 targets for 69 yards in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers.
items.text: Mumpfield saw a team-high five targets and turned them into a team-leading 69 yards in one of the more dominant performances of the season. Despite the seemingly close score, the Rams jumped out to an early 13-3 lead while holding the Packers to only 44 total offensive plays run from scrimmage. The inability of the Packers to move the football resulted in additional time of possession for the Rams, which they used to notch 47 rush attempts to just 23 Matthew Stafford pass attempts, eight of which were directed at the backfield duo of Blake Corum and Kyren Williams. items.title: Kyren Williams rushed 12 times for 46 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers, adding 19 yards on four receptions.
items.text: Williams now operates as the clear change of pace option and preferred back in passing situations, with recent reports pointing to consistent pain due to a turf toe injury likely the culprit in the shifting dynamics of the backfield in Los Angeles. Either way, Williams spent most of the second half on the sideline as Corum set career highs in attempts (32) and yards (184) while becoming the first back in the Sean McVay era to reach 30 carries. items.title: Blake Corum rushed 32 times for 184 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers, adding 21 yards on two receptions.
items.text: The 184 yards on the ground easily set a new career high for the veteran back and his 32 carries marked the first time in the Sean McVay era where a single back ran the football 30 or more times, a mark that had not been reached since Todd Gurley over a decade ago. His trip to paint stretched his streak of touchdowns to five games while he also went over 100 yards for the second straight contest. items.title: Matthew Stafford completed 16-of-23 passes for 140 yards and an interception in the Rams’ 26-13, Week 12 win over the Packers.
items.text: The two sides traded blows in the first half as the Packers came from behind to knot the game at 13 heading into the break, with Stafford leading three consecutive scoring drives to start the game for the first time this season. That was also the first time the Packers had allowed an opponent to score on three consecutive drives to start a game this season, but the departure of Christian Watson in the second quarter due to a concussion completely took the wind out of their sails in the second half.
